text.content:
Bytopia is the great forge of the Wheel: two worlds smothered in factories, foundries and deep mines whose output equips armies across known space. Whole fleets haul ore in and finished goods out. The system is otherwise exhausted; three gas giants and two rocky worlds were dismantled long ago, leaving only drifting metal scaffolds. Industrial smog fills the sphere so densely that the void has a faint, pressurized haze. There are no magical hazards and physics behaves normally, but ship traffic is so heavy it is a danger in itself, kept in check by superb controllers aided by Virtual Intelligence. Ore shipments get priority over nearly everything.

Both surviving planets are wrapped in artificial rings that serve as freight docks and mass drivers, with space elevators hanging down to the surface; waste is fired into the sun. Dothion is a rust-red world of self-contained arcologies, monorails and walkways, whose people rarely leave their neighbourhoods and vacation in crowded artificial parks. Shurrock builds restricted goods such as weapons, military armour, lockpicks and spelljammer parts; its workers are watched and searched constantly, and visitors are confined to designated zones under threat of lethal policing.

@UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceSquat0000]{Squats} and @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceHuman0000]{Humans} make up most of the population, which mostly lives indoors and may never see daylight. @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceHalfling0]{Halflings} are numerous too, scraping by on wits and leftovers in the depths of the factory-cities, while @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceGnome0000]{Gnomes} tend the oldest and most arcane machinery to keep it running. Native wildlife is nonexistent; the only animals are a few beasts of burden used in certain factories and pets owned by the wealthy.

Ring 0 is the oldest surviving scaffold, the overbuilt prototype from the first planet stripped bare, now circling a worthless slag core. Independent traders celebrate finished runs at Absolute Zero, an inflatable, glass-walled bar there that has been wrecked and rebuilt repeatedly; its @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceEldarin00]{Eldarin} exile bartender, Moondog, relishes the risk. The derelict Last Ruby Rays of Dawn lost its crew to its own deadly cargo a century ago and now drifts inside a vast exclusion zone, yet lights and signals are rumoured to come from it.

GWOTT Headquarters is the city-sized seat of the Great Wheel's trade and tariff authority, which polices commerce and contraband across the Wheel and stays apart from Sigil and the Factions. Its reclusive chief is Eclipse, and it reportedly fields Exalt teams that bend local laws. Solar Observatory #14 secretly watches a station orbiting impossibly close to the sun, unharmed by solar plasma and possibly Syrneth; activity aboard seems to be rising, but its orbit will decay into the sun within a generation.

Story Master only: adventure seeds for this sphere.

A Shurrock factory holds a legion of Warstriders, giant walking war machines able to conquer whole spheres; bidding opens next week, and suspiciously detailed security leaks invite a heist. Miners digging a new geofront on Dothion broke into an artificial complex of black metal halls, strange power sources and stasis banks, then went silent as something hateful seemed to wake.

Two senior GWOTT agents have defected, claiming a cabal of merchants and nobles secretly steers the agency; internal reports hint the rogues are powerful Exalts. Meanwhile, the hidden mind-control agent Shurrock laces into food, water and entertainment to keep workers content is starting to drive long-term users into murderous rampages.
